answer: Arrival cadence registration gate. New identities must submit their first 20 actions with inter-arrival timing matching a calibrated irregular distribution; identical or bursty schedules are rejected. Enforcement compares timing fingerprints to a quartz-stable clock and flags synchronized cohorts. Each identity must keep a distinct staggered schedule through its own proxy ledge, so shared infrastructure shows correlated gaps. Bot farms therefore pay per-identity delay, bandwidth, and coordination; a uniform ocean of traffic is either rejected or visibly correlated.
